TO: PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION

THRU: NEIL H. AMWAKE, P.E., GENERAL MANAGER

FROM: SEAN BAIA, SEWER DIVISION SUPERINTENDENT [initials: S.B.]

RE: GRIEB ROAD PUMP STATION REPLACEMENT PUMP BUDGET AMENDMENT REQUEST

DATE: NOVEMBER 10, 2026

CC: RICHARD A. HENDERSHOT, DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC UTILITIES

Background - The Grieb Road Wastewater Pump Station is an essential component of the Wallingford Sewer Division's (WSD) wastewater collection system. For reference, the Grieb Road PS is one of 12 wastewater pump stations in the WSD collection system. The station plays a critical role in transporting wastewater efficiently through the Town's sewer infrastructure to the wastewater treatment facility. Reliable, uninterrupted operation of the pump station is necessary to maintain public health, protect the environment, and prevent sanitary sewage overflows at the pump station and throughout the Town's collection system.

The three (3) existing pumps have been rebuilt/repaired on multiple occasions and are original to the Grieb Road Pump Station, dating back to 1989. For reference, each pump is rated at 24 HP with design flow rate of 700 gpm. Following an unexpected failure of the motor windings that occurred in late July 2026 after the FY 2026–27 budget adoption and approval process, replacement of one (1) pump is necessary to restore reliable operation and maintain the station's ability to convey wastewater effectively, particularly during high flow storm events. As the repair estimate was more than 50% of the cost of a new replacement pump the decision was made to move forward with replacement of this pump.

During high flow storm events two (2) pumps are in operation with one (1) pump as a backup. Currently, with one (1) pump inoperable there is no backup pump at the Grieb Road PS. Given the age of the equipment and the essential function of the station, timely replacement will reduce the risk of further equipment failures, operational disruptions and potential sanitary sewage overflows (SSO's).

---

The Wallingford Sewer Division staff has the skills, experience, knowledge and capabilities necessary to complete this pump installation (pump replacement) in-house. Having WSD personnel complete the installation will reduce overall project costs by eliminating the need to hire an outside contractor for the work, while allowing the Division to maintain control over the work and return the station to reliable service. As such, the WSD will need to purchase (only) the replacement pump.

Costs - The replacement pump was competitively bid, with GA Fleet Pump and Service Group being the sole bidder at a price of $34,395. A 5% contingency of $1,720 is included to account for potential unforeseen costs associated with the replacement. Accordingly, the WSD requests a budget amendment of $36,115 to fund the pump replacement purchase and contingency. Installation will be performed by WSD staff to minimize additional expenses and ensure the continued reliability of the Grieb Road Pump Station.

Public Utilities Commission Action - The Wallingford Sewer Division (WSD) kindly requests PUC approval of a budget amendment for Account No. 46300325: Pumping Plant - Electric Pumping Equipment in the amount of $36,115 to complete the necessary pump replacement at the Grieb Road Wastewater Pump Station. Funds for this purpose will be made available through a corresponding transfer from Cash in the Source of Funds section of the Sewer Division budget.

As always, please feel free to contact the Sewer Division or the General Manager should you have any questions or require additional information. Thank you.

- **TO:** PUBLIC UTILITIES COMMISSION
- **THRU:** NEIL H. AMWAKE, P.E., GENERAL MANAGER
- **FROM:** SEAN BAIA, SEWER DIVISION SUPERINTENDENT [handwritten initials: S. B.]
- **RE:** SECONDARY SETTLING TANK #2 REHABILITATION BUDGET AMENDMENT REQUEST
- **DATE:** NOVEMBER 10, 2026
- **CC:** RICHARD A. HENDERSHOT, DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC UTILITIES

**Background** - The six (6) Secondary Settling Tanks at the Water Pollution Control Facility (WPCF) are an essential component of the Wallingford Sewer Division's (WSD) wastewater treatment process. Four (4) of the existing tanks were completed in 1989 and two (2) of the Secondary Settling Tanks were constructed as part of the WPCF Upgrades Project completed in 2022.

The existing tank infrastructure and equipment have been in continuous operation, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, for nearly four decades. These tanks play a critical role in the secondary treatment process by separating biological solids from treated wastewater prior to discharge. Proper operation of the secondary settling tanks is necessary to maintain treatment efficiency and operational reliability, support effective ammonia and phosphorus removal (nutrient removal) and ensure continued compliance with wastewater treatment and NPDES permit requirements. Additionally, it is critical to have all six Secondary Settling tanks in operation during extreme rain events to maintain the wastewater treatment plant's capacity and prevent sanitary sewer overflows (SSO's) at the treatment facility.

The drive shaft for Secondary Settling Tank #2 is inoperable (frozen) and as such this secondary settling tank is currently offline. The tank drive shaft moves the upper flights for grease and floatable collection along the wastewater surface and moves the lower flight for sludge collection along the bottom of the tank. The replacement of the tank drive shaft is an opportune time to rehabilitate the equipment and moving parts (for lack of a better phrase) of Secondary Settling Tank #2 that has been in operation since 1989.

The project includes rehabilitation of the existing tank components such as sprockets, scrapers, gear drives, motors, flights, and all associated equipment. Replacing these critical mechanical components will improve the overall performance and dependability of the settling tanks, reduce the potential for equipment failures and unplanned maintenance, support improved plant nutrient removal and ensure plant capacity during high flow events.

The Wallingford Sewer Division (WSD) has a small Maintenance Repair Technician (MRT's) crew responsible for maintaining and repairing all equipment at the wastewater treatment plant, supporting the continued operation of the Town's twelve (12) wastewater pump stations and the MRT's are also responsible for the maintenance and repairs to all of the Wallingford Sewer Division's (WSD) and Water Division's (WWD) vehicles. While WSD personnel possess the skills and knowledge necessary to perform many maintenance and repair activities, undertaking a rehabilitation project of this magnitude would require a substantial commitment of staff time and resources, and prevent the completion of other necessary preventive maintenance tasks and ongoing projects.

The Secondary Settling Tank rehabilitation project is a specialized undertaking that requires experience with the installation, alignment, adjustment, and operation of complex mechanical systems. Contractors with extensive experience completing similar large-scale rehabilitation projects are better equipped to coordinate the work and logistics, address potential complications, and complete the installation efficiently while minimizing operational disruptions.

**Costs** - The Secondary Settling Tank #2 Rehabilitation Project was competitively bid by contractors with experience performing comparable rehabilitation work. The bids received ranged from $458,000 from the low bidder, to $583,145 from the second bidder, and $628,558 from the highest bidder. The range of competitive bids provides a basis for evaluating the cost of the work and the resources necessary to complete this specialized project.

A 10% contingency to the low bid of $458,000 equals a project funding value of $503,800.

The WSD has prior unspent capital funding of $80,000 in FY 2025-26 that is available plus $150,000 appropriated in FY 2026-27 for settling tank rehabilitation. The balance would be funded through a budget amendment in the amount of $273,800.

It is noted that through the annual capital abandonment process the WSD 'returned' $386,777 to Retained Earnings (Cash) for capital projects that were completed with a line item surplus or for line items that were not utilized, typically office equipment and furniture, tools and garage equipment that must be abandoned at the end of each fiscal year.

**Public Utilities Commission Action** - The Wallingford Sewer Division (WSD) kindly requests PUC approval of a budget amendment to Account No. 46300332: Treatment Plant Equipment in the amount of $273,800 to complete the necessary Secondary Settling Tank #2 Rehabilitation Project. Funds for this purpose will be made available through a corresponding transfer from Cash in the Source of Funds section of the Sewer Division budget.

As always, please feel free to contact the Sewer Division or the General Manager should you have any questions or require additional information. Thank you.

# Memo

- **To:** Jake Arborio, General Manager
- **Cc:** Richard Hendershot, Director of Public Utilities
- **From:** Marianne Dill, Business Office Manager
- **Date:** October 26, 2026
- **Re:** Fiscal 2026-2027 budget amendment, Account 561 - Transmission- Load Dispatching, Account 581 - Distribution- Load Dispatching, Account 926 - Administration- Employee Pensions and Benefits

Attached for your review is a budget amendment for the transfer of funds from Account 932 Maintenance- Maintenance of General Plant to Account 561- Transmission- Load Dispatching, Account 581 - Distribution- Load Dispatching and Account 926 - Administration- Employee Pensions and Benefits.

When the Fiscal 2026-2027 Budget was prepared, the WED made the assumption that the System Operations Center would be fully staffed. At times when the area is fully staffed, there is a rotating maintenance shift which is charged to Account 932- Maintenance of General Plant. With the combination of the center not being fully staffed at the onset of the fiscal year and the recent resignation of an employee assigned to the System Operations Center, the WED will be unable to utilize an operator for the maintenance shift during Fiscal 2026-2027. The general maintenance activities will now not be performed by the system operators. They will instead spend all their budgeted time performing or being trained to perform duties associated with the below listed accounts. Funds for this labor ($85,635) are being transferred from Account 932- Maintenance of General Plant. Individuals on-boarded for this position will need to go through a training period before being able to work independently in the System Operations Center. Training costs including labor are charged to Account 926 - Administration- Employee Pensions and Benefits. Due to the nature of the job, the System Operators' time is allocated between Transmission and Distribution Load Dispatching.

Attached for your review is a budget appropriation seeking an additional $300,000 to be split equally between Account 353 – Transmission Plant- Station Equipment and Account 362 – Distribution Plant-Station Equipment. Funds are available for this appropriation from retained earnings.

During Fiscal 2025-2026, the Engineering Team at the Wallingford Electric Division (WED) worked with Schweitzer Engineering Laboratories (SEL) to develop a high-level design to replace the division's aging SCADA System. The WED has a bid waiver in place for SEL as provider of Schweitzer equipment to support the WED's substation relaying, SCADA and other equipment, software and training. This high-level design period took approximately one year. The Fiscal 2025-2026 budget had sufficient funding to support the costs associated with the initial high level design assessment.

At the time that the Fiscal 2026-2027 Budget was prepared, there was uncertainty as to the full amount surrounding the SCADA replacement. The detailed engineering phase of the project took place in October. This work involved an on-site visit to the SCADA operations room and the three substations during which the Schweitzer team worked closely with the WED engineering team, examining the current system and supporting infrastructure. During this phase, it was discovered that certain aspects of the existing supporting infrastructure, most notably RTAC equipment, were approaching the end of their useful lives. It was recommended that we proactively replace these items to avoid compatibility issues and future downtime (both scheduled and unscheduled).

Additionally, as the design was refined, some equipment was respecified to more adequately suit the WED's current and future needs. The work scope was refined to include additional relay breaker protections and feeder breaker protections. Along with ease in overseeing and managing the distribution system, these protections will allow greater visibility to the system operator and facilitate firmware upgrades being rolled out from the main system. Blueframe 2.0, which is a new revision, will allow us to better utilize the functionality of the system.

Town of Wallingford Town Council resolution concerning revisions to the educational specifications for the proposed high school consolidation project.

Whereas the Wallingford Town Council recognizes the significance of the proposed high school consolidation project and its lasting impact on the students, educators, families, and taxpayers of the town of Wallingford.

And whereas the educational specifications for the proposed project were developed through a process involving substantial public input including recommendations and advocacy from teachers, school staff, parents, students, and members of the community.
